content: The following individuals and their professional roles contributed to the development of the WHO guidelines on self-care interventions for health and well-being: 1. Kenya Lisa Noguchi serves as the Director of Maternal and Newborn Health at Jhpiego in Baltimore, Maryland, USA. 2. Gina Ogilvie is a Professor at the Faculty of Medicine, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, Canada. 3. Ash Pachauri is the Director of the Centre for Human Progress in New Delhi, India. 4. Michelle Remme is the Research Lead at the International Institute for Global Health, United Nations University, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. 5. Jayalakshmi Shreedhar is a Senior Technical Expert in Accountability and Media Engagement at the Resource Group for Education and Advocacy for Community Health in Chennai, India. 6. Leigh Ann van der Merwe is a Coordinator for Social, Health, and Empowerment in East London, South Africa. 7. Sheryl van der Poel is an independent consultant based in Geneva, Switzerland. 8. Allen Wu, a co-chair, is a Professor and Director at the Centre for Public Health Research, Medical School, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China. External contributors to the systematic reviews for the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) system included experts from the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health in Baltimore, Maryland, USA, such as Caitlin Kennedy and Ping Teresa Yeh, supported by Kait Atkins, Shannon King, Jingjia (Cynthia) Li, and Dong Keun Rhee. Additionally, Nandi Siegfried, a methodologist and independent clinical epidemiologist from Cape Town, South Africa, contributed to the methodology. The External Review Group included professionals such as: Faysal Al Kak from the American University of Beirut Medical Centre, Lebanon. Jack Byrne from Trans-Action in Auckland, New Zealand. Georgina Caswell from the Global Network of People Living with HIV in Cape Town, South Africa. Tyler Crone from the Athena Network in Seattle, Washington, USA. Eva Deplecker, a leader in reproductive health and sexual violence at Médecins Sans Frontières, Belgium. Austen El-Osta from the Self-Care Research Unit at Imperial College London, UK. Joanna Erdman from the Health Law Institute, Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University, Halifax, Canada. Mariangela Freitas da Silveira from the Graduate Programme in Epidemiology, Universidade Federal de Pelotas, Brazil. Patricia Garcia, former Minister of Health in Peru and a member of the School of Public Health, Universidad Cayetano Heredia, Lima, Peru. Roopan Gill, Co-Founder and Executive Director of the Vitala Global Foundation, Canada. James Hargreaves from the Centre for Evaluation, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, UK. Rei Haruyama from the National Centre for Global Health and Medicine, Tokyo, Japan. Denis Kibira from the Coalition for Health Promotion and Social Development, Kampala, Uganda. Amy Knopf from the University of Indiana, Indianapolis, USA. Oswaldo Montoya from the MenEngage Alliance, Washington, DC, USA. Ulysses Panisset from the University of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Michael Tan from the College of Social Sciences and Philosophy, University of the Philippines, Quezon City, Philippines. Viroj Tangcharoensathien from the Ministry of Public Health, Thailand. Tarek Turk from the Syrian Arab Red Crescent Hospital, Ministry of Health, Damascus, Syria. Julián Vadell Martinez, a researcher and project manager at the International Council of Nurses, Paris, France. Sten Vermund from the Yale School of Public Health, Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, USA. Zawora Rita Zizien from the Universal Health Care Division, Ministry of Health, Burkina Faso. Representatives from United Nations agencies also contributed, including: Pascale Allotey, Director of the International Institute for Global Health, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Layal Barjoud, Technical Specialist at the Defeat-NCD Partnership, Geneva, Switzerland. Ruben Brouwer, Human Rights Advisor at the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Geneva, Switzerland. Emily Christie and Luisa Cabal, Senior Advisers at the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS, Geneva, Switzerland. Shaffiq Essajee, Senior Advisor on HIV at UNICEF, New York, USA. Kenechukwu Esom, Policy Specialist on Human Rights, Law, and Gender at the United Nations Development Programme, New York, USA. Maribel Almonte, Programme Director at the International Agency for Research on Cancer, Lyon, France. Petra ten Hoope-Bender, Technical Adviser on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights at the United Nations Population Fund, Geneva, Switzerland. Etienne Langlois, Team Lead for Evidence and Knowledge at the Partnership for Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health, Geneva, Switzerland. Sameera Maziad Al Tuwaijri, Global Lead for Population and Development at the World Bank, Washington, DC, USA. Tim Sladden, Senior HIV Adviser at the United Nations Population Fund, New York, USA. Damilola Walker, Senior Advisor and Global Team Lead for Adolescents and HIV at UNICEF, New York, USA. David Wilson, Program Director and Global Lead for Decision and Delivery Science at the World Bank, Washington, DC, USA. These experts and organizations played critical roles in the development, review, and dissemination of the WHO guidelines, ensuring a comprehensive and inclusive approach to self-care interventions for health and well-being.
